subtitle: Early ARPANET maps showing geographic and logical network layout

tldr.problem: The ARPANET community needed current maps showing the network's physical layout and logical connections.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 616 distributed two maps: a geographic map showing where network nodes were located and a logical map showing how they were connected.

today: RFC 616 is a historical document that captured the ARPANET's topology in January 1974.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
RFC 616 presents the latest ARPANET maps as of January 1974. It consists of two maps: a geographic map showing the physical locations of ARPANET nodes across the United States, and a logical map showing how those nodes are interconnected.

The original RFC was a document containing two one-page illustrations. These maps provided network operators and researchers with a visual reference for understanding the ARPANET's topology at a specific point in time.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC is just two pictures: one that shows where each computer was, and one that shows which computers were plugged into each other.

sections.title: Maps from January 1974
sections.content:
The geographic map displayed the network nodes' physical locations, helping operators understand which institutions were connected to the ARPANET and where they were distributed. The logical map showed the communication paths, revealing how data could flow between nodes through the network's hardware connections.

Major sites included MIT, Stanford, Lincoln Laboratory, and others participating in the early network research effort.
sections.plainLanguage: The maps showed which universities and research centers were on the network, and which ones could send messages to which other ones.

sections.title: Historical Significance
sections.content: These maps captured the ARPANET's state in early 1974, five years after the network's initial deployment. They serve as a historical record of the network's growth and evolution during its formative years.
sections.plainLanguage: This shows what the early internet looked like when it was just getting started.
